question.leadin: Ozan Kilinc ("KILL-inch") was jailed by a court in this country for publishing articles sympathetic to a banned party.
question.text: Name this country, where insulting the country or the government is illegal under Article 301.
question.clue: This country was permitted to remilitarize a waterway by the Montreaux Convention.

swap.leadin: The Golden Horn cuts into this city and was once spanned by a large chain to prevent enemy ships from getting in.
swap.text: Name this Turkish city that was previously named Byzantium and Constantinople.
swap.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

question.text: In the 1910s and 20s, the Young Turks perpetrated a genocide on this ethnic group, in which the Ottoman Empire forced this group from their homeland. The modern Turkish government refuses to identify the event as a genocide.
question.answerHtml: Armenians (accept Armenian genocide or Armenian Holocaust, but do not prompt on Holocaust)
question.clue: Sophene and Commagene were ruled by their Orontid dynasty.

swap.leadin: A huge amount of impressive building projects were designed by this ruler's architect, Sinan.
swap.text: Name this son of Selim the Grim, who won the Battle of Mohacs [Moe-HOTCH] but was less successful in conquering Malta and also led an unsuccessful siege of Vienna.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [or Suleiman the Lawgiver or Suleiman I; prompt on “Suleiman”]
swap.clue: This man's forces defeated the Knights Hospitaller during the 1522 Siege of Rhodes, but Spanish intervention prevented a second victory during the Great Siege of Malta.

question.text: Name these units of infantry composed of former Christians converted to Islam by the devsirme system.
question.clue: When these people were eliminated, the closely-associated sect of Bektashi Sufism was banned.

swap.leadin: Many of those who orchestrated this event were assassinated during Operation Nemesis.
swap.text: Identify this event in which over a million people of a certain Caucasian nationality were forcibly resettled and killed, perpetrated by the Ottoman Empire during World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide (accept equivalents like Armenian Massacre; prompt on “Great Crime” or “Medz Yeghern”)
swap.clue: Henry Morgenthau Sr. wrote a firsthand account of this event, which began on "Red Sunday" with a deportation of intellectuals.

question.text: This sultan and rumored lover of Radu the Handsome presided over the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453. His armies thereby ended the Byzantine empire.
question.answerHtml: Mehmet II [or Mehmet the Conqueror; or Mehmet el-Fatih; accept “Mehmed” for “Mehmet”]
question.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

swap.text: The Janissaries were disbanded before this period of 19th-century reforms, which began with the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. Its modernizing provisions included ending a tax on non-Muslims and nationalizing the census.
swap.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

question.leadin: He died at the siege of Szigetvar after resuming warfare in Hungary in 1566.
question.text: Name this Ottoman sultan, the son of Selim the Grim, who defeated the aforementioned Hungarians at the great battle of Mohacs forty years earlier.
question.clue: He employed Sinan as the chief architect, married Roxelana, and was often called "kanuni."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about rebellious janissaries.
swap.text: The janissaries revolted for a final time in 1826, after which they were finally disbanded in this event that saw most janissary troops executed, exiled, or imprisoned.
swap.clue: This massacre of soldiers perpetrated by Mahmud II.

question.leadin: It was the first campaign fought by the combined New Zealand-Australian forces called ANZAC.
question.text: Name this campaign of 1915 into early 1916 in which the British and French attempted to capture Istanbul by taking a certain peninsula in Turkey.
question.answerHtml: Gallipoli Campaign [or Dardanelles Campaign; or Çanakkale Savaşları; or Çanakkale Wars]
question.clue: Three attempts were made to take Krithia during this campaign after a successful landing at Cape Helles.

swap.text: This son of the Kayi tribe leader Ertugrul founded the Ottoman Dynasty after throwing off the yoke of the Seljuks.
swap.answerHtml: Osman I [or Osman Gazi; or Osman Bey; or Othman I El-Gazi; or Osman Sayed II]
swap.clue: This figure's father Ertugrul was a member of the Kayi tribe, and along with troops known as the Ghazi warriors, this man was victorious over George Mouzalon and his Byzantine forces at the Battle of Bapheus.

question.text: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.
question.answerHtml: Pasha [accept Three Pashas or İsmail Enver Pasha or Mehmed Talaat Pasha or Ahmed Cemal Pasha or Djemal Pasha]
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.text: The Janissaries were first organized in the 1360s under the rule of this first Ottoman sultan, who was killed at the battle of Kosovo.
swap.clue: A Serbo-Magyar coalition that invaded his territory was crushed at the Battle of the Maritsa River.

question.text: Soon after the Auspicious Incident, the Ottoman army was modernized during this wider initiative. The introduction of paper money and post offices, as well as units called vilayets, were among the changes introduced during this initiative.
question.clue: This period begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber.

swap.text: Attempts to collect reparations from Germany had been suspended in 1932 after a conference at this city. A 1923 treaty here recognized the state of Turkey and was the final treaty ending World War I.
swap.clue: The large Greek population still living in Anatolia after World War I was forcibly exchanged with Turks in Greece by the terms of a convention signed in this city during negotiations to replace the Treaty of Sevres ("SEV").

question.leadin: An Abkhazian-born statesman with this name promoted the 'ulama's separation of powers in The Surest Path and visited Paris with the Fundamental Pact's author Bin Diyaf.
question.text: Give this name of a reformer who created the Sadiki lycee ("lee-SAY") under Sadok Bey. A beylerbeyi ("BAY-lar-bee") of Algiers who went by this Islamic name captured Hafsid Tunis after the Zayyanids killed his brother Oruc ("oh-ROOCH").
question.answerHtml: Hayreddin [or Hayrettin, Khair al-Dīn, Khayr ad-Dīn, or Kheireddine; accept Hayreddin Barbarossa, Khair al-Dīn Barbarus, Hızır Hayrettin Pasha, or variants; accept Hayreddin Pasha, Khayr ad-Dīn Pāshā t-Tūnisiyy, Khair al-Dīn al-Tunsi, or Tunuslu Hayreddin Paşa; prompt on Barbarossa, Barbarus, Khiḍr, Khiḍr, Hızır, mevlâna, or sultânü’l mucâhid by asking “what Islamic name did he generally use?”]

swap.text: Under Ahmed III, the Ottomans began to use Greek administrators of this family to govern most of their western provinces. They were named for the Greek quarter of Constantinople and included men like Alexander Yspilantis who served as Voivode of Wallachia and Moldavia.
swap.clue: In the 18th century, this class of Greek merchant families dominated Ottoman government positions such as Grand Dragoman of the Fleet and Hospodar of Moldavia. They were named after a Greek neighborhood in Istanbul.

question.text: This overall commander of Ottoman forces at Beersheba later received a surname drawn from the two 1921 battles where he forced invading Greeks to retreat. He was the successor of Ataturk as the second President of Turkey.
question.clue: The implementer of the Turkish surname law, Mustafa Kemal, took the surname Ataturk, while this "National Chief" who succeeded him took his surname from a town where he fought during the Greco-Turkish War.

swap.leadin: Cardinal Julian Cesarini, the legate of Pope Eugene IV, was killed during this battle, but a more important casualty was King Wladyslaw III of Poland.
swap.text: Name this 1444 battle, in which the Ottoman Turks defeated the combined armies of Poland and Hungary, who were attempting to liberate Bulgaria.
swap.clue: This battle began with Franco Talotsi and Michael Szilagyi successfully defending their flanks from attacks by the Akincis and Sipahis.
